reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents Coinbase Earn as an educational program involving lessons and quizzes, with cryptocurrency rewards tied to participation. The narration is framed as informational rather than investment advice, and the invitation-based eligibility condition does not establish that every viewer can receive the asset.

citations.quote: Users can go to a page, watch educational videos relating to those assets, and then complete tasks about those assets. In return, they'll earn cryptocurrency.
Coinbase Earn allows users to earn cryptocurrencies while learning about them in a simple and engaging way.
Anybody can now come to a webpage, click some buttons, earn some cryptocurrency, and understand what this thing is all about.
Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.

opening.argument: This is presented as a direct low-barrier acquisition offer: viewers are told they can receive cryptocurrency by watching videos and completing tasks. The required actions are deliberately simple, and the stated reward is tied to completing them, making the content function as a solicitation to participate rather than merely an explanation of crypto. The invitation screen reinforces that the viewer is being directed into an earn flow, not just offered general information.

citations.quote: Users can go to a page, watch educational videos relating to those assets, and then complete tasks about those assets. In return, they'll earn cryptocurrency.
Introducing Coinbase Earn: A New Way to Earn Crypto While You Learn Crypto

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material educational does not remove the central inducement. The described lessons and tasks are the mechanism for obtaining crypto, and the visible invitation says viewers are invited to earn 0x. The disclaimer addresses investment advice, but this argument concerns a reward linked to participation, not a recommendation to buy or hold an asset.

citations.quote: In return, they'll earn cryptocurrency.
Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The reward-action relationship is real, but these excerpts do not show deception or an illegitimate claim. They describe educational viewing and asset-related tasks, while the program also limits earning through invitations. The material therefore shows a promotional educational benefit, not proof that the promised reward is fraudulent.

citations.quote: You'll know if you're eligible if you receive an invite to Coinbase earn in your inbox.
Even if you're not yet eligible to earn cryptocurrency on that page, you'll be able to view the educational content

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: cryptocurrency is framed as something that can be obtained simply by clicking buttons, with no mining or purchase required, and the viewer is directed to a dedicated earn page. The offer uses an unusually easy acquisition path for a digital asset and pairs it with a prominent invitation to earn 0x. Even without a deposit request, that combination can make the reward sound effortless while leaving the actual conditions and amount unclear.

citations.quote: This is because one can — in theory — earn
Anybody can now come to a webpage, click some buttons, earn some cryptocurrency, and understand what this thing is all about.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a deposit does not resolve the concern created by the easy-reward framing. Saying anyone can click buttons and earn crypto presents acquisition as nearly frictionless, while the visible call to earn 0x supplies the concrete inducement. The informational disclaimer does not clarify the reward's amount, fulfillment, or practical limitations.

citations.quote: click some buttons, earn some cryptocurrency
Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited language expressly qualifies the broad claim with 'in theory,' and the program explains that eligibility requires an invitation. The supplied material also shows lessons and a quiz, so the workflow is not merely unexplained clicking. These excerpts do not establish that the reward is deceptive, unavailable, or misrepresented.

citations.quote: one can — in theory — earn
You'll know if you're eligible if you receive an invite to Coinbase earn in your inbox.

opening.argument: Although the presentation adopts an educational tone, its operational role is promotional: Coinbase introduces its own branded program, directs viewers to its earn page, and presents a specific asset reward for completing the program's activities. The lesson content is the funnel through which viewers are steered toward participation. Branding, an invitation to earn 0x, and a linked destination make this more than neutral education about cryptocurrency.

citations.quote: That’s why Coinbase is launching Coinbase Earn with tasks related to asset education
Learn more about Coinbase's mission here: https://www.coinbase.com/mission

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference description of lessons and quizzes actually supports the promotional reading: those educational elements are embedded in a branded Coinbase Earn campaign and connected to receiving 0x. Saying the video is not investment advice does not make it neutral, because the requested participation is earning through Coinbase's program rather than buying an investment.

citations.quote: Coinbase Earn allows users to earn cryptocurrencies while learning about them
This content, and any information contained therein, does not constitute a recommendation by Coinbase to buy, sell or hold any security

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and scam are not equivalent. The cited material identifies Coinbase's program and explains its educational purpose, but it does not show that the program misrepresents its conditions or takes money from participants. The reward is tied to lessons and tasks, and earning eligibility is expressly invitation-based.
